transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... I just can’t stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It's really bothering me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just don't see it that way. I feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work for, or the nurses, or even the people at my church notice when they look at me. I just can't stop focusing on it, and I don't know what to do.

Do you find yourself performing any specific actions, such as constantly checking the mirror, touching the area, or seeking reassurance from others, to try to deal with how you feel about your jaw and neck?

Yeah, I do. Especially before I leave for work or a meeting. I just... I keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my collar and trying to arrange my hair around my neck to hide it. And then, even after I walk away, I'll pull out my phone and take another look in the camera just to check it again. 

Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange, too. Honestly, doing all that... it's actually made me late more than once.
How much does this constant checking and worrying about your appearance impact your ability to get through your day or interact with the people around you?

Well, it gets in the way more than I'd like to admit. At work, I've actually passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on supervisory roles. I just... I worry too much that people will be staring right at my face and neck the whole time. And I've fallen behind on my paperwork, too, because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to make myself look presentable before I can focus on anything else. 

It affects my personal life, too. I've stopped going to my book club and my walking group lately. It just feels like too much work to get ready and try to hide it, so I just stay home instead.
Have you ever sought out or considered any medical, surgical, or cosmetic procedures to fix your jaw or neck?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've never gone to a doctor or a surgeon about it. I haven't looked into any kind of surgery or procedures like that to fix it. I just try to cover it up myself.
Do you ever find yourself picking, scratching, or rubbing your skin in that area to try and smooth it out or make it look better?

No, I don't really do that. I mean, I might touch my neck sometimes just to adjust my collar or my hair, like I mentioned, but I don't sit there picking at the skin or rubbing it to try and smooth it out. It's more about trying to cover the shape of it, not changing the skin itself.

When you worry that people are staring at your jaw or neck, do you feel that they are judging you specifically because of how that area looks, or are you more generally worried about being embarrassed or scrutinized in social situations?

I think it's specifically about my jaw and neck. I mean, I don't really get nervous just from being around people or talking to them. It's really just that I'm convinced they're looking right at that part of my face and thinking how awful it looks. If I didn't have this problem with my jaw and neck, I don't think I'd be worried about being judged at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a preoccupation with a perceived defect in her physical appearance (jaw/neck) that is not observable or appears only slight to others. This preoccupation leads to repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, camera checking, reassurance seeking, camouflaging) and significant impairment in social and occupational functioning. She explicitly denies that her distress is due to general social anxiety, pointing specifically to the perceived physical flaw.
